questions.question: Figure 1 shows part of the curve C with equation y = 1/(x + 2). State the equation of the asymptote of C that is parallel to the y-axis.
steps: The denominator is zero when x + 2 = 0.
So the vertical asymptote is x = -2.

questions.question: Factorise fully x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x.
steps: Take out the common factor x: x(x^2 + 4x + 4).

questions.question: On a copy of Figure 1, add a sketch of y = x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x, and state clearly the coordinates of each point where this curve cuts or meets the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: Curve passes through (0, 0) and touches the x-axis at (-2, 0); no other axis intercepts
steps: y = x(x + 2)^2 from part (b).
Set y = 0: x = 0 or x = -2 (double root), so the curve meets the x-axis at (0, 0) and touches it at (-2, 0).
y-intercept: x = 0 gives y = 0, the same point (0, 0).
The curve is negative for x < 0 except touching at -2, and positive for x > 0.

questions.question: Hence state the number of real solutions of (x + 2)(x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x) = 1, giving a reason for your answer.
steps: Divide by (x + 2): x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x = 1/(x + 2), so solutions are the intersections of y = x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x with C.
For x > -2, C is positive and the cubic is only positive for x > 0; they cross once for x > 0.
For x < -2, the cubic goes from -infinity up to 0 and C goes from 0 down to -infinity, so they cross once.
So there are 2 real solutions.

questions.question: A curve C has equation y = f(x) where f(x) = 2(x + 1)(x - 3)^2. Sketch a graph of C, showing the coordinates of the points where C cuts or meets the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: Crosses x-axis at (-1, 0), touches at (3, 0), crosses y-axis at (0, 18)
steps: Roots: x = -1 (single, crosses the axis) and x = 3 (double, touches the axis).
Leading coefficient is 2 > 0, so the curve rises from the left and rises to the right after touching (3, 0).

questions.question: Write f(x) = 2(x + 1)(x - 3)^2 in the form ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d, where a, b, c and d are constants to be found.
steps: Multiply by 2: 2x^3 - 10x^2 + 6x + 18.

questions.question: Hence, using algebra, find the equation of the tangent to C at the point where x = 1/3. Calculator solutions are not acceptable.
steps: The tangent is the horizontal line y = 512/27.

questions.question: Figure 4 shows part of the curve C with equation y = f(x), where f(x) = (3x - 2)^2 (x - 4). Deduce the values of x for which f(x) > 0.
steps: (3x - 2)^2 is never negative, and is zero only at x = 2/3, where f(x) = 0.
So the sign of f(x) is the sign of (x - 4).
f(x) > 0 when x > 4.

questions.question: Expand f(x) = (3x - 2)^2 (x - 4) to the form ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d, where a, b, c and d are integers.
steps: Collect terms: 9x^3 - 48x^2 + 52x - 16.

questions.question: The line l passes through the y-intercept of C and is parallel to the x-axis. l cuts C again at P and Q. Using algebra, find the length PQ in the form k sqrt(3), where k is a constant to be found.
steps: x = 0 is the y-intercept, so P and Q satisfy 9x^2 - 48x + 52 = 0.
PQ = difference in x = 4sqrt(3)/3, so k = 4/3.

questions.question: On Diagram 1, sketch a graph of the curve C with equation y = 6/x, x not 0.
questions.answer: Hyperbola in quadrants I and III with asymptotes the x-axis and y-axis
steps: y = 6/x has asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0.
It lies in quadrants I (x > 0) and III (x < 0).
Draw both branches, approaching the axes but never meeting them.

questions.question: The curve C is transformed onto the curve with equation y = 6/(x - 2), x not 2. Fully describe this transformation.
questions.answer: A translation of 2 units in the positive x direction
steps: Replacing x by x - 2 shifts the graph horizontally.
So the transformation is a translation by the vector (2, 0).

questions.question: The curve y = 6/(x - 2), x not 2, and the line y = kx + 7 intersect at exactly two points P and Q. Given that the x coordinate of P is -4, find the value of k.
steps: Substitute into the line: -1 = k(-4) + 7.

questions.question: Using algebra, find the coordinates of point Q, where the curve y = 6/(x - 2) and the line y = 2x + 7 meet at Q.
steps: Factorise: (2x - 5)(x + 4) = 0, giving x = 5/2 or x = -4.
x = -4 is P, so Q has x = 5/2 and y = 2(5/2) + 7 = 12, giving Q = (5/2, 12).

questions.question: Figure 1 shows y = f(x), with a minimum at (3, -1) and passing through (0, 0) and (6, 0). On separate diagrams, sketch y = f(2x), showing the coordinates of any intercepts with the x-axis and any minimum or maximum points.
steps: f(2x) is f(x) squeezed horizontally by a factor 1/2.
Zeros of f move from x = 0 and x = 6 to x = 0 and x = 3.
The minimum moves from (3, -1) to (1.5, -1).

questions.question: On separate diagrams, sketch y = f(x + p), where p is a constant and 0 < p < 3. On each diagram show the coordinates of any points where the curve intersects the x-axis and of any minimum or maximum points.
questions.answer: Zeros at (-p, 0) and (6 - p, 0); minimum at (3 - p, -1); y-intercept (0, f(p))
steps: f(x + p) is f(x) translated p units to the left.
Zeros: x + p = 0 or 6, so x = -p and x = 6 - p.
Minimum moves to (3 - p, -1).
The y-intercept is (0, f(p)).

questions.question: The curve C1 has equation y = f(x), where f(x) = (4x - 3)(x - 5)^2. Sketch C1, showing the coordinates of any point where the curve touches or crosses the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: Crosses x-axis at (3/4, 0), touches at (5, 0), crosses y-axis at (0, -75)
steps: Roots: x = 3/4 (single, crosses) and x = 5 (double, touches).
Leading coefficient 4 > 0, so the curve rises to the right.

questions.question: Hence or otherwise (i) find the values of x for which f(x/4) = 0, and (ii) find the value of the constant p such that y = f(x) + p passes through the origin.
steps: (ii) The origin requires f(0) + p = 0.

questions.question: A second curve C2 has equation y = g(x), where g(x) = f(x + 1). (i) Find, in simplest form, g(x), leaving the answer factorised if you wish. (ii) Hence, or otherwise, find the y-intercept of C2.
steps: Replace x by x + 1: 4(x + 1) - 3 = 4x + 1, and (x + 1) - 5 = x - 4.

questions.question: Sketch the curve with equation y = -k/x, where k > 0 and x not 0.
questions.answer: Hyperbola in quadrants II and IV with asymptotes the x-axis and y-axis
steps: Since k > 0, y = -k/x has the opposite sign to x.
It lies in quadrant II (x < 0, y > 0) and quadrant IV (x > 0, y < 0).
Asymptotes are the axes.

questions.question: On a separate diagram, sketch the curve with equation y = -k/x + k, where k > 0 and x not 0. State the coordinates of the point of intersection with the x-axis and, in terms of k, the equation of the horizontal asymptote.
questions.answer: Crosses x-axis at (1, 0); horizontal asymptote y = k
steps: Set y = 0: -k/x + k = 0, so x = 1, giving (1, 0).
The graph of -k/x is shifted up by k.
The horizontal asymptote is y = k.

questions.question: Find the range of possible values of k, with k > 0 and x not 0, for which the curve y = -k/x + k does not touch or intersect the line y = 3x + 4.
steps: Set -k/x + k = 3x + 4 and multiply by x: 3x^2 + (4 - k)x + k = 0.
No intersection requires discriminant < 0: (4 - k)^2 - 12k < 0.
Expand: k^2 - 20k + 16 < 0.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows y = f(x) with minimum P(-1, 0), maximum Q(3/2, 2) and the only asymptote y = 1. On separate diagrams sketch y = f(x) - 2, stating the coordinates of the maximum and minimum points and the equation of the asymptote.
steps: Shift f(x) down by 2.
Minimum moves from (-1, 0) to (-1, -2).
Maximum moves from (3/2, 2) to (3/2, 0).
Asymptote moves from y = 1 to y = -1.

questions.question: Using Figure 1 (minimum P(-1, 0), maximum Q(3/2, 2), asymptote y = 1), sketch y = f(-x), stating the coordinates of the maximum and minimum points and the equation of the asymptote.
steps: f(-x) is f(x) reflected in the y-axis.
Minimum (-1, 0) reflects to (1, 0).
Maximum (3/2, 2) reflects to (-3/2, 2).
The asymptote y = 1 is unchanged.

questions.question: The curve C has equation y = 4/x + k, where k is a positive constant. Sketch a graph of C, stating the equation of the horizontal asymptote and the coordinates of the point of intersection with the x-axis.
questions.answer: Horizontal asymptote y = k; crosses x-axis at (-4/k, 0)
steps: y = 4/x + k has asymptotes x = 0 and y = k.
Set y = 0: 4/x = -k, so x = -4/k, giving (-4/k, 0).
Branches lie in quadrants I and III, shifted up by k.

questions.question: The line with equation y = 10 - 2x is a tangent to C. Find the possible values for k.
steps: Set 4/x + k = 10 - 2x and multiply by x: 4 + kx = 10x - 2x^2.
Rearrange: 2x^2 + (k - 10)x + 4 = 0.
Tangent means a repeated root: discriminant (k - 10)^2 - 32 = 0.
k - 10 = +/- sqrt(32) = +/- 4sqrt(2), so k = 10 +/- 4sqrt(2), both positive.

questions.question: Given 0 < k < 4, sketch on separate axes the graph of y = (2x - k)(x + 4)^2, showing the coordinates of any points where the graph crosses or meets the axes, leaving coordinates in terms of k where appropriate.
questions.answer: Crosses x-axis at (k/2, 0); touches at (-4, 0); crosses y-axis at (0, -16k)
steps: Roots: x = k/2 (single, crosses) and x = -4 (double, touches).
For x > k/2 the curve is positive, rising to infinity.

questions.question: On separate axes, sketch y = k/x^2 for 0 < k < 4, showing the coordinates of any points where the graph crosses or meets the axes, leaving coordinates in terms of k where appropriate.
questions.answer: No intercepts with either axis; asymptotes are x = 0 and y = 0; positive for all x not 0
steps: k/x^2 is never zero, so it does not meet the x-axis.
It is undefined at x = 0, so it does not meet the y-axis.
Both branches lie above the x-axis, approaching x = 0 and y = 0 as asymptotes.

questions.question: State, with a reason, the number of roots of (2x - k)(x + 4)^2 = k/x^2.
steps: Roots are intersections of the two graphs from part (a).
For x < 0 the cubic is never positive while k/x^2 is positive, so no intersections there.
For 0 < x < k/2 the cubic is negative, so no intersections.
For x > k/2 the cubic increases from 0 to infinity while k/x^2 decreases, so they meet once: 1 root.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows y = f(x), passing through P(-4, 6), Q(-1, 6), R(2, 6) and S(3, 6). Using Figure 1, find the range of values of x for which f(x) < 6.
steps: The curve is below 6 to the left of P, and between Q and R, and to the right of S.
Left of P: x < -4.
Between Q and R: -1 < x < 2.
Right of S: x > 3.

questions.question: State the largest solution of the equation f(2x) = 6.
steps: 2x = 3 gives the largest solution x = 3/2.

questions.question: (i) Sketch y = f(-x) on Figure 1 and state the coordinates to which P, Q, R and S are transformed. (ii) Hence find the set of values of x for which f(-x) >= 6 and x < 0.
steps: f(-x) reflects the graph in the y-axis: P(-4, 6) to (4, 6), Q(-1, 6) to (1, 6), R(2, 6) to (-2, 6), S(3, 6) to (-3, 6).
With t = -x: -4 <= -x <= -1 gives 1 <= x <= 4, which is excluded by x < 0.
With 2 <= -x <= 3 gives -3 <= x <= -2, which satisfies x < 0.

questions.question: Figure 5 shows y = f(x) where f(x) = sqrt(x), x > 0, with P(9, 3) on the curve. On Diagram 1, sketch and clearly label y = f(2x) and y = f(x) + 3, showing on each graph the coordinates of the point to which P is transformed.
questions.answer: f(2x) passes through (9/2, 3); f(x) + 3 passes through (9, 6)
steps: f(2x) = sqrt(2x) is a horizontal stretch by factor 1/2, so P(9, 3) maps to (9/2, 3).
f(x) + 3 = sqrt(x) + 3 is a vertical translation up 3, so P maps to (9, 6).
Label both curves and the transformed points on Diagram 1.

questions.question: The graph of y = f(2x) meets y = f(x) + 3 at point Q. Show that the x coordinate of Q is the solution of sqrt(x) = 3(sqrt(2) + 1).
steps: At Q: f(2x) = f(x) + 3, so sqrt(2x) = sqrt(x) + 3.
sqrt(2x) = sqrt(2) sqrt(x), so sqrt(2) sqrt(x) - sqrt(x) = 3.
sqrt(x)(sqrt(2) - 1) = 3, so sqrt(x) = 3/(sqrt(2) - 1) = 3(sqrt(2) + 1), as required.

questions.question: Hence find, in simplest form, the coordinates of Q.
steps: Square both sides: x = 9(sqrt(2) + 1)^2 = 9(3 + 2sqrt(2)) = 27 + 18sqrt(2).
